answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 19 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. The walnut multiplier is published, charged in quill, and lotus lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 4661 identities would post 1851 proofs and burn roughly 34 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
